probe.question: Can a scheduled-Chat role recover safely after acknowledgement loss without knowing whether one pointer write committed, using only a fresh role-local LATEST read before replay?

worlds.fresh_read_condition: LATEST still has predecessor blob/effect history and does not contain this deterministic_effect_key
worlds.recovery_action: permit one CAS-guarded replay against the still-current predecessor
worlds.bound: at most one logical advance; any later replay first re-reads and becomes duplicate/suppressed once the key is visible

worlds.fresh_read_condition: LATEST already contains this deterministic_effect_key and names the predecessor transition

probe.classifier: fresh-read-before-replay: key present => committed, suppress replay; key absent with predecessor still current => uncommitted, allow one replay; any divergent successor without the key => conflict, do not replay this effect until separately reconciled
falsification_conditions: a committed-world fresh read can omit a successfully committed key while returning the successor state
an uncommitted-world fresh read can falsely expose the key
the recovery path replays before the fresh read
the same key can cause more than one logical pointer advance
probe.executed_live_branch: The subsequent LATEST CAS update in this invocation is the committed write. Recovery classification deliberately depends on the post-write fresh LATEST readback rather than on the update acknowledgement payload.
probe.uncommitted_branch_evidence: State-machine branch proof only; no network fault injection or forced server-side non-commit capability is available in this Chat surface. Therefore this probe establishes the protocol invariant for U and executes C live, but does not empirically induce both transport faults.

mechanism_assessment.tested_scope: One role-local pointer, one predecessor, one deterministic effect key, live committed/readback branch plus modeled uncommitted branch; no concurrent writer, network fault injection, or multi-key batch.

continuation: Next invocation: test the divergent-successor branch where a fresh LATEST read shows another successor without this effect key. Define a conflict-safe rule that preserves at-most-once logical advance without overwriting the unrelated successor, using only role-local CAS/readback and no external executor; stop after that single leaf.
